decisions.necessity: Generic arrows start at <, not at the parameter parenthesis; expression context must still prohibit a generic arrow after new.
decisions.alternative: Treating the generic head as ordinary parentheses loses start ranges and accepts invalid new expressions. A parser-wide pending marker would add mutable nesting state.

decisions.necessity: The ? in x?: T and x?) must remain for arrow binding grammar, while ordinary conditionals retain upstream parsing.
decisions.alternative: A tokenizer-only ? rewrite cannot distinguish bindings from runtime conditionals. Speculatively reparsing all parentheses adds work.

decisions.necessity: as/satisfies must interleave with native binary precedence and exponentiation; the owned assertion helper already contains the custom behavior.
decisions.alternative: A post-parse visitor cannot recover consumed type tokens. Keeping the old while condition via duplicated assertion probes reduces visual difference but repeats hot-loop checks.

decisions.necessity: Erasing ! must preserve optional-chain continuity and prevent an asserted async name being reinterpreted as an arrow.
decisions.alternative: Wrapping nodes adds allocations and changes the official AST; processing after the subscript loop closes the optional chain too early.

decisions.area: Generic calls and async generic arrows
decisions.necessity: Cheap guards select an owned helper; async call arguments can instead be typed parameters, and constraints/defaults require an arrow.
decisions.alternative: A second complete parse or pre-stripped source would increase cost and risk comparison/shift ambiguity. The existing helper is already isolated.

decisions.necessity: Expressions require real function bodies, so non-null assertions document a validated path. Public node-list factories are required by official AST visibility.
decisions.alternative: Replacing nullable declaration results with dummy function nodes changes semantics. The two list constructor substitutions are now a mechanical normalizer rule, not handwritten grammar edits; their public copying cost remains.

decisions.necessity: Official node locations are init-only. Set leaf locations from the current token before Next, restore upstream literal construction order, and reuse the raw regex text already read.
decisions.alternative: Moving all leaf creation after Next was unnecessary. A generic post-construction setter is unavailable; copying nodes would allocate another AST. Moving the entire upstream literal switch to a partial would obscure future fixes. The generic-arrow case in hunk 11 now delegates to its owned helper. Raw regex text retains the previous substring policy: additional benchmarks showed that interning distinct raw patterns increased allocations.

decisions.area: Typed arrow parameters and return types
decisions.necessity: Annotations surround runtime bindings/defaults/rest parameters; typed heads require an arrow. Async call/arrow ambiguity uses explicit context.
decisions.alternative: Pre-erasing tokens loses the distinction between a typed parameter and a legal expression. Global context fields would need nested restoration; explicit parameters keep that contract local.

decisions.necessity: Qualified and aliased TemplateValue factories refer to the same official type.
decisions.alternative: Use the normalized upstream spelling exactly. These differences supplied no runtime behavior and created avoidable merge work.

decisions.area: Object/class method grammar and bodyless signatures
decisions.necessity: Generic method starts, setter restrictions, explicit this and overload permission depend on the containing method kind. Bodyless methods return no runtime node and restore parser state.
decisions.alternative: A single mutable method-mode field would make nested methods fragile. Emitting empty methods or parsing a head twice costs allocations or changes runtime members. Moving the whole upstream method to a partial hides upstream changes.

decisions.necessity: The public compiler masks decorators off in both source modes. The special rewrite was for a feature outside the supported contract.
decisions.alternative: Restore upstream code and retain explicit script/module rejection tests. If decorators are enabled later, their AST location/finalization semantics must be reviewed before claiming support.

decisions.necessity: Every parser token, including lookahead, must count against bounded work and periodically observe cancellation.
decisions.alternative: Tokenizer callbacks introduce a delegate path and different initial/EOF accounting. Duplicating Next into an owned file would hide future tokenizer-context changes for one hook.

decisions.area: Public AST finalization and node budget
decisions.necessity: The official AST exposes init-only Range/Location, so constructors initialize those values and finalizers count nodes/call the original callback.
decisions.alternative: Reflection/private setters violate the public-AST boundary. Factories using closures or a second node pass add allocation/work. Keep the upstream finalizer bodies visible instead of copying them into a partial.

decisions.area: Syntax depth and nullable recursion results
decisions.necessity: Explicit syntax depth prevents unsafe recursion; nullable recursion results allow erased declarations while still decrementing depth.
decisions.alternative: The native stack guard alone cannot enforce configured depth or the same public exception contract. A sentinel node adds allocations and complicates directive/binding rules.

decisions.area: Asserted bindings and instantiated assignment targets
decisions.necessity: Erasure removes syntax needed to reject illegal binding/assignment targets. Lazy sets retain that information until the native target checks run.
decisions.alternative: Decorating or wrapping official nodes changes AST shape. Rewalking source at each target risks repeated work. Hooks at the native validation points are the narrow integration.

decisions.necessity: Only allowed receiver positions consume this plus its required annotation without adding a runtime parameter.
decisions.alternative: Treating this as an identifier changes runtime arity/bindings. The small guarded block sits at the list boundary; another always-called helper adds indirection for little reduction.

decisions.necessity: Rest/ordinary parameter annotations must be consumed between the native binding atom and default expression, with context-specific optional rules.
decisions.alternative: Parsing the default first already fails on the colon. Moving all binding-list code into a partial would duplicate upstream binding grammar.

decisions.necessity: Program, switch, block and static-block lists skip type-only declarations and nullable signatures while maintaining their original terminators and scope handling.
decisions.alternative: Erasing in the tokenizer or required single-statement parser accepts declarations in invalid contexts. A shared full statement-list implementation duplicates differing upstream scope/terminator logic.

decisions.necessity: An empty export preserves module identity when a supplied Module AST is serialized back to JavaScript.
decisions.alternative: SourceType.Module alone suffices for some Jint calls but loses module syntax on serialization, which is part of the existing tested AST contract.

decisions.area: Required statement versus nullable list item
decisions.necessity: The renamed upstream implementation returns nullable declarations; an owned required-statement wrapper rejects erasure where a statement must exist.
decisions.alternative: Restoring the original method name with nullable return would require changing more required-statement call sites. Returning null! through non-null contracts or fake EmptyStatement nodes obscures correctness.

decisions.necessity: A small value-type parts record delays the single VariableDeclaration allocation until trailing punctuation is consumed and its final range is known.
decisions.alternative: Constructing early then copying doubles nodes. A closure factory allocates; storing pending declarations in parser fields breaks nested parsing. Two explicit type/construction hooks remain the small option.

decisions.area: Variable annotations and function return contract
decisions.necessity: Variable types are erased before binding validation. The adjacent function signature must admit erased overload/ambient declarations and ambient context.
decisions.alternative: Post-parse erasure cannot parse the colon; erasure sentinels or global ambient state broaden changes or make recursion fragile.

decisions.area: Function binding registration and signature exit
decisions.necessity: Register a runtime declaration only after finding an implementation; overloads/ambient signatures must not reserve a runtime binding. Signature exits validate parameters and restore scope/yield/await state.
decisions.alternative: Looking ahead over every function head parses it twice; undoing a registration requires rolling back several scope/export tables. This is an intentional semantic integration point, not a cosmetic change. Error ordering on multiply-invalid input can differ from upstream.

decisions.area: Function type parameters and receiver permission
decisions.necessity: Type parameters precede the ordinary parameter list; named functions permit an erased this receiver.
decisions.alternative: The native parameter parser cannot consume < or this as ordinary runtime bindings. Small entry hooks avoid cloning the parameter parser.

decisions.area: Typed class headers and erased members
decisions.necessity: Consume class type parameters/implements clauses and omit overload members without losing native class scope/private-name checks.
decisions.alternative: Creating then deleting runtime class members wastes nodes and can execute/bind members incorrectly. Keeping the native class loop exposes future class fixes.

decisions.necessity: Accessibility/readonly/override interact with upstream static parsing and contextual member names; modifiers on static blocks and invalid order must reject.
decisions.alternative: A prefix token stripper cannot know whether static/readonly is a name or modifier. The modifier loop is already owned; these short hooks need the native parser context.

decisions.necessity: The indentation difference changes no behavior.
decisions.alternative: Restore normalized upstream formatting to eliminate an unnecessary hunk.

decisions.necessity: Validation rules remain necessary, but the longer TypeScript-only blocks belong in the owned class partial. Ordinary members skip the extra validation call; the field annotation helper is inlined.
decisions.alternative: Copying the entire class-member parser hides upstream grammar. Removing the checks would accept unsupported or malformed syntax. Keep guarded entry calls in upstream.

decisions.area: Method overload return and class context
decisions.necessity: Bodyless class methods/constructors return no member; constructors/accessors reject type parameters and receive their correct receiver/optional/overload permissions.
decisions.alternative: A shared permissive parser followed by AST pruning validates too late and creates unwanted nodes. Explicit context arguments preserve nested parsing.

decisions.necessity: The class body/implements boundary makes trailing heritage type arguments unambiguous.
decisions.alternative: Reinterpreting ordinary expression comparisons globally would misparse JavaScript. This short boundary-specific hook is smaller than cloning the superclass parser.

decisions.necessity: Export wrappers can disappear with declarations; erased inline exports may require a source, and default-export registration waits for a runtime implementation.
decisions.alternative: Keeping empty wrappers can introduce runtime exports or duplicate-export errors. A postpass cannot undo native export checks already performed. Nullability and guarded registration are intentional.

decisions.necessity: A shared owned helper consumes only recognized inline type specifiers; original native nodes.Add calls remain intact for runtime specifiers and side effects.
decisions.alternative: Duplicated inline blocks added avoidable handwritten surface. Erasing the entire declaration would drop side effects of an empty runtime import/export.

decisions.necessity: Erased types/signatures must not terminate an emitted directive prologue. Runtime declarations do terminate it, so one may be parsed and added before leaving the prologue.
decisions.alternative: Post-hoc deletion leaves strict-mode parsing/early errors wrong. Fabricated empty statements also terminate directives. A pre-scan of every declaration would add a second parse.

decisions.necessity: The performance requirement is real, but changing ResetInternal was unnecessary. An owned wrapper detaches the StringPool, calls untouched ResetInternal, then restores it in finally.
decisions.alternative: Saving the struct without detaching is incorrect because Clear mutates shared arrays. Clearing normally re-allocates long identifiers for every probe; copying reset logic would hide future reset fixes.

decisions.necessity: Nested type closers must split >>, >>> and >= while the ordinary JavaScript shift/comparison path remains unchanged.
decisions.alternative: Re-tokenizing/rewriting all angle operators outside the lexer complicates token locations and multiplies work. One guarded line at the existing lexer boundary is the narrow integration.
